title: Scanning for secrets
purpose: Looks for credential-shaped strings before you commit, push or post them: tokens, keys, `password=` values, credentials in URLs, private keys and long random strings. It uses the same rules toil's audit log redacts with, plus an entropy check, and exits with 1 when it finds anything, so a hook or a pipeline can stop on it.
inputs: A file, a folder (skipping what `.gitignore` ignores), stdin, `--text`, or your staged or unstaged changes with `--diff`. A known false positive goes in `.toil/secrets-allow` by its fingerprint, or in the file `--allow-file` names.
verifies: Every finding is read again at the position reported, with the same rule finding it there; every preview is checked to hide the secret's middle; and each file was read to its size on disk.
limits: The secret itself is never printed, logged or returned. Files it couldn't read (binary, too large, no permission) are listed, never skipped. It scans line by line, so a secret split across two lines (other than a private key) isn't found, and a diff covers the workspace only. `--diff` runs git.
